intro.title: Interactive science simulations
intro.lead: Mathematics, physics, astronomy and cosmology to explore in the classroom. Every simulation runs in the browser, with no installation and no internet connection.

featured.title: Featured
featured.subtitle: A selection of simulations to start exploring.

physics.title: Physics
physics.subtitle: Fundamental phenomena, from mechanics to modern physics.

astronomy.title: Astronomy

astronomical-horizon.title: Astronomical Horizon

equatorial-coordinates.title: Equatorial Coordinates

sky-calendar.title: Astronomical Calendar

lunar-calendar.title: Lunar Calendar

ptolemy-sun-celestial-sphere.desc: The apparent path of the Sun on the celestial sphere according to ancient astronomy.

ptolemy-ecliptic-3d.title: Ecliptic in the Ptolemaic Model
ptolemy-ecliptic-3d.desc: Visualize the ecliptic in the Ptolemaic model.

ptolemy-geocentric-orbits.title: Orbits in the Ptolemaic Model
ptolemy-geocentric-orbits.desc: Visualize planetary orbits in the Ptolemaic model.

ptolemy-epicycles-3d.title: Retrograde Motion in the Ptolemaic Model
ptolemy-epicycles-3d.desc: See in 3D how epicycles produce the retrograde motion of the planets.

ptolemy-deferents-epicycles.title: Deferents & Epicycles
ptolemy-deferents-epicycles.desc: Ancient mathematical mechanism to explain retrograde planetary motion.

ptolemy-venus-phases.title: Phases of Venus in the Ptolemaic Model

copernicus-earth-sun-system.desc: Basic orbital dynamics between Earth and the Sun.

copernicus-ecliptic-3d.desc: Visualize how the Sun's apparent position changes in the Copernican model.

copernicus-moon-phases.title: Moon Phases
copernicus-moon-phases.desc: 3D simulation of Sun-Earth-Moon positions and how they generate moon phases seen from Earth.

copernicus-retrograde-3d.title: Apparent Retrograde Motion
copernicus-retrograde-3d.desc: Elegant explanation of apparent planetary backtracking from a heliocentric perspective.

copernicus-venus-phases.title: Phases of Venus in the Copernican Model
copernicus-venus-phases.desc: How the heliocentric model correctly predicts the phases of Venus.

copernicus-elliptical-orbits.title: Elliptical Orbits
copernicus-elliptical-orbits.desc: Kepler's laws and the actual motion of planets in ellipses.

solar-system-creator.title: Solar System Creator
solar-system-creator.desc: Gravity sandbox: launch planets and watch how their orbits interact.

exoplanets.title: Exoplanet Explorer
exoplanets.desc: Search for exoplanets in our galaxy and discover their characteristics.

stellar-map.title: Stellar Distances
stellar-map.desc: 3D visualization of stars nearest to the Sun. Navigate among them!

spectra.title: Common Spectra
spectra.desc: Interactive catalog of emission and absorption spectra for various elements.

distance-luminosity.title: Distance & Luminosity
distance-luminosity.desc: How a star's light diminishes with the square of the distance.

black-hole.title: Black Hole
black-hole.desc: Visualize the characteristics of a black hole.

universe-expansion.title: Expansion of the Universe
universe-expansion.desc: Simulate Hubble's Law and how space itself stretches dragging galaxies.

cmb.title: Cosmic Microwave Background
cmb.desc: Visualize the cosmic microwave background in 3D.

cosmological-parameters.title: Cosmological Parameters
cosmological-parameters.desc: Determine density parameters from SNIa data.

universe-evolution.title: Evolution of the Universe
universe-evolution.desc: Cosmic timeline from the Big Bang to the present day.

super-kamiokande.title: Super-Kamiokande
super-kamiokande.desc: Explore the Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector and how Cherenkov light reveals passing particles.

tambo.title: TAMBO
tambo.desc: Explore TAMBO, the tau-neutrino observatory proposed in a valley of the Peruvian Andes.

about.title: About
about.what_text: A collection of interactive physics, astronomy, and cosmology simulations created to support teaching. Each simulation is self-contained and works offline.
about.notice_text: These simulations are intended for educational purposes only and have not been scientifically validated. The models include simplifications and approximations, so their results must not be used for research or technical decisions.
about.unofficial_text: This is a personal, independent project. Simulations depicting scientific experiments or collaborations (for example, Super-Kamiokande or TAMBO) are the author’s own outreach recreations: they are not official products of those collaborations, are not endorsed by them, and do not represent the position of the author’s institution. All names and logos mentioned belong to their respective owners.
about.offline_text: You can download the whole repository from GitHub (Code → Download ZIP) and use it without internet. Simulations marked with the server icon must be opened through a local server, because browsers block loading modules and files when an HTML file is opened by double-clicking. The repository includes a ready-to-use one:
about.offline_single: If you only need one simulation, copy its folder; if it has the server icon, also place start-server.py inside it and run it there.
about.license_text: The code is released under the MIT License. If you use these simulations in academic work, please cite them using the CITATION.cff file in the repository.
